傳.note: 傳 chuán relates to passing something on. 傳統 chuántǒng means “tradition; traditional.”
傳.memory: A person 亻 stands beside 專. Imagine traditions being passed from person to person as a memory cue.

parts.label: 亻
parts.name: person component
parts.description: Person component in 傳: strokes 1–2. A person 亻 stands beside 專. Imagine traditions being passed from person to person as a memory cue.

parts.label: 專
parts.name: right component
parts.description: Right component in 傳: strokes 3–13. A person 亻 stands beside 專. Imagine traditions being passed from person to person as a memory cue.

統.note: 統 tǒng appears in 傳統 chuántǒng, “tradition; traditional.” Learn the whole word rather than guessing from the parts.
統.memory: Threads 糹 stand beside 充. Think of traditions linked together like threads as a visual mnemonic.

parts.label: 糹
parts.name: thread component
parts.description: Thread component in 統: strokes 1–6. Threads 糹 stand beside 充. Think of traditions linked together like threads as a visual mnemonic.

parts.label: 充
parts.name: right component
parts.description: Right component in 統: strokes 7–12. Threads 糹 stand beside 充. Think of traditions linked together like threads as a visual mnemonic.

輕.note: 輕 qīng means “light,” the opposite of heavy. 年輕 niánqīng is the whole word for “young.”
輕.memory: 車 is on the left and 巠 is on the right. Keep the two seven-stroke blocks balanced.

parts.label: 車
parts.name: vehicle component
parts.description: Vehicle component in 輕: strokes 1–7. 車 is on the left and 巠 is on the right. Keep the two seven-stroke blocks balanced.

parts.label: 巠
parts.name: right component
parts.description: Right component in 輕: strokes 8–14. 車 is on the left and 巠 is on the right. Keep the two seven-stroke blocks balanced.

部.note: 部 bù refers to a part or section. 大部分 dàbùfen means “most; the greater part.”
部.memory: 立 over 口 forms the left block 咅; the narrow 阝 is on the right. Compare 陪, where 阝 is on the left.

parts.label: 咅
parts.name: left component
parts.description: Left component in 部: strokes 1–8. 立 over 口 forms the left block 咅; the narrow 阝 is on the right. Compare 陪, where 阝 is on the left.

parts.label: 阝
parts.name: right component
parts.description: Right component in 部: strokes 9–10. 立 over 口 forms the left block 咅; the narrow 阝 is on the right. Compare 陪, where 阝 is on the left.

u40-questionword-totality.title: All-inclusive question words with 都 / 也
u40-questionword-totality.pattern: Question word + 都 + … / Question word + 都 or 也 + 不／沒…
u40-questionword-totality.explanation: Question words can form total inclusion: 誰都 'everyone', 哪裡都 'everywhere', 什麼都 'everything', 什麼時候都 'anytime', and 怎麼 + V + 都 'whichever way'. For total exclusion, use question word + 都 or 也 + 不／沒, with the negative after 都/也. Both 都 and 也 are valid in negative total-exclusion. The pattern forms questions for this pattern with 嗎.

examples.pinyin: Zuótiān wǒ nǎlǐ dōu méi qù.

u40-questionword-totality.remember: Affirmative: question word + 都. Negative: question word + 都/也 + 不/沒. Put the negative after 都/也.

u40-more-less-verb.title: Do more / do less with 多／少 + Verb
u40-more-less-verb.pattern: 多 / 少 + Verb (+ 一點 + Object)
u40-more-less-verb.explanation: Before a verb, 多 means do more than planned/usual and 少 means do less/fewer than planned/usual. This differs from earlier quantity uses. The pattern can refer to past or future events, and 一點 often modifies the object.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng duō xué yìdiǎn Zhōngwén.
examples.meaning: I want to study a little more Chinese.

u40-more-less-verb.remember: Put 多 or 少 before the action verb to mean do more or less than planned/usual.

u40-everything-source.note: This preview is now formalized as the question-word totality pattern.

u40-anytime.meaning: Any time is fine for me.
u40-anytime.note: Affirmative totality with 什麼時候都.

u40-anyway.meaning: Any way of going is fine.
u40-anyway.note: 怎麼 + V + 都 gives all-inclusive 'whichever way'.

u40-nobody.note: Negative total exclusion: 誰 + 也 + 沒.

u40-nowhere.pinyin: Zuótiān wǒ nǎlǐ dōu méi qù.
u40-nowhere.note: Negative total exclusion: 哪裡 + 都 + 沒.

u40-nothing.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān shénme yě bù xiǎng chī.
u40-nothing.meaning: I don't want to eat anything today.
u40-nothing.note: Negative total exclusion with 什麼 + 也 + 不.

u40-dialogue-q.text: 臺灣人過生日是不是都吃這些東西？
u40-dialogue-q.pinyin: Táiwān rén guò shēngrì shì bú shì dōu chī zhèxiē dōngxi?
u40-dialogue-q.meaning: Do Taiwanese people all eat these things for birthdays?
u40-dialogue-q.note: Conversation continuation. 是不是 is comprehension-only until Unit 41.

u40-young-source.text: 現在大部分年輕人過生日不吃這些東西了。
u40-young-source.pinyin: Xiànzài dàbùfēn niánqīng rén guò shēngrì bù chī zhèxiē dōngxi le.
u40-young-source.meaning: Nowadays, most young people don't eat these things for birthdays anymore.

u40-dialogue-tail.text: 那麼，你們過生日吃什麼呢？
u40-dialogue-tail.pinyin: Nàme, nǐmen guò shēngrì chī shénme ne?
u40-dialogue-tail.meaning: Then, what do you eat for birthdays?
u40-dialogue-tail.note: Culture summary: traditional birthdays could follow the lunar calendar, while the Gregorian calendar is common today. Early-life celebrations include one month and one year; major decades include 60, 70, and 80. On a first birthday, the zhuāzhōu 'grabbing' custom has the child choose from several objects, traditionally interpreted as a clue to future character or profession. 那麼 also carries the connective sense 'then / in that case' in the sentence above.

u40-less-buy.text: 最近沒錢，應該少買東西。
u40-less-buy.pinyin: Zuìjìn méi qián, yīnggāi shǎo mǎi dōngxi.
u40-less-buy.meaning: I've had little money lately, so I should buy fewer things.

u40-more-study.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng duō xué yìdiǎn Zhōngwén.
u40-more-study.meaning: I want to study a little more Chinese.
